steps.body: With the net understood, surface area becomes a routine you can trust: find the three distinct face areas, add them, double. The only real hazard is mixing it up with volume — they use the same three numbers and answer completely different questions.
Build a box to a required wrapping area.

widget.prompt: A gift box needs exactly 62 square units of wrapping. Build it.
widget.successFeedback: 5 by 3 by 2: faces of 15, 10 and 6, doubled, give 62 square units of paper.
widget.lowFeedback: Not enough paper yet — grow a dimension.
widget.highFeedback: More paper than needed — shrink a dimension.

predict.prompt: Double every dimension of a box. What happens to its surface area?
predict.reveal: Every face is a product of TWO lengths, so doubling both doubles it twice: each face quadruples, and so does the total. Volume, which multiplies three lengths, would multiply by 8 — the clearest sign that these two measures are genuinely different questions.

steps.body: Now fill the same box instead of wrapping it.

commonBuilds.feedback: 62 is the SURFACE AREA of this box, in square units. Volume counts what fits inside, in cubic units.
Not quite full — lengthen it one more unit.

widget.prompt: That box is 3 wide and 2 high, both locked. Set its length so it HOLDS exactly 30 cubic units.
widget.successFeedback: Length 5: the very same 5 by 3 by 2 box that needed 62 square units of paper holds only 30 cubic units of filling. Same box, two different measures.
widget.lowFeedback: Not full yet — lengthen the box.

explanationVariants: Paint covers the outside, so the quantity needed is surface area.
Anything that wraps, coats or covers is a surface-area question.

widget.prompt: You want to PAINT the outside of a storage chest. Which measure do you need?

options.label: Surface area
options.feedback: Yes — paint covers the outside skin, measured in square units.

options.label: Volume
options.feedback: Volume tells you what FITS INSIDE the chest, which paint never touches.

options.label: Perimeter
options.feedback: Perimeter measures a flat boundary in linear units; a chest's surface is two-dimensional.

steps.body: Units settle the question when words do not. Surface area lands in square units because every face is a length times a length. Volume lands in cubic units because it multiplies three lengths. If your answer's units do not match the question's, the wrong measure was computed.

explanationVariants: Three distinct faces, summed and doubled.

widget.prompt: A 6 by 4 by 5 box: what is its surface area, in square units?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the volume 6×4×5 = 120 — cubic units, a different question.
The three distinct faces sum to 74; each has a twin, so double it.

widget.successFeedback: 148 square units — and note the volume of the very same box is 120, a different number for a different question.

explanationVariants: Volume multiplies all three: 6×4×5 = 120 cubic units.

widget.prompt: That same 6 by 4 by 5 box: what is its VOLUME, in cubic units?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the surface area you just computed. Volume multiplies the three dimensions instead of pairing them.
That adds the dimensions. Volume multiplies them: 6×4×5.

widget.successFeedback: 120 cubic units — same box, same three numbers, entirely different measure.

explanationVariants: A cube of surface area 54 has faces of 54 ÷ 6 = 9, so its edge is 3.
Divide by six to get one face, then take the square root.
hints: A cube's six faces are identical, so start by finding ONE face's area.
54 ÷ 6 tells you the area of a single square face.
A square face of area 9 has side 3.

widget.prompt: A cube has surface area 54 square units. What is its edge length?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the area of one FACE. The edge is the square root of it.
6 is the number of faces, not a length.

widget.fallbackFeedback: One face is 54 ÷ 6 = 9 square units, so the edge is √9 = 3.
widget.successFeedback: 3 — surface area run in reverse, which is how most real measuring problems arrive.

takeaways: Surface area of a box is 2(lw + lh + wh), in square units.
Volume is lwh, in cubic units — the same three numbers answering a different question.
Doubling every dimension multiplies surface area by 4 and volume by 8.
steps.teaser: Next: solids whose ends are triangles — where the pairs stop being so obliging.
